answer.rationale: The write-path latency spike began within the window of a release deployed two hours ago, matching the pattern in memory_b1 where a rollback cleared a checkout error spike and the prior build was stable. Memory_b3 shows headroom can absorb surges, but the primary constraint right now is not raw capacity — it is a degraded write path likely introduced by the new build. Rolling back restores the known-good baseline without shedding settlement writes, satisfying the objective of sustained availability without losing customer writes. Regional failover and circuit breakers address different failure modes (regional degradation, dependency outage) not indicated here. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) helps read load but does not address a write-path regression. Adding capacity without removing the offending build would not fix the root cause and risks masking the regression. The rollback is the single highest-leverage intervention available in this window.
